## 1. Executive summary

### 1.1 Hypothesis scorecard

All numbers come from the locked-set final run unless the row says otherwise.

| ID | Question | Result | Key numbers |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Does ML (RK4/leapfrog + certified safety scale, FTLE feature cost counted) stay within tolerance on ≥90% of orbits AND need fewer evaluations than RK45 and DOP853 on ≥50% of orbits? | NOT supported | Within tolerance: 96.3% (pass). Cheaper than adaptive: 0.0% / 0.0% / 0.0% / 0.0% of orbits (RK45 spec / RK45 cal / DOP853 spec / DOP853 cal; needs ≥50%). Median ML cost (feature cost included) is 55× to 193× the adaptive cost. |
| H1'a | Same, but model trained without FTLE, prediction cost charged (added after seeing development data) | NOT supported | Within tolerance: 96.1%. Cheaper than adaptive in all four comparisons: 0.0%, 0.0%, 0.0%, 0.0%. (Before prediction cost is charged, 29.3% / 20.3% of orbits are cheaper against the calibrated RK45 / DOP853 only.) |
| H1'b | Same, but compared with the best single certified fixed step per integrator (added after seeing development data) | Supported (post-hoc comparator) | ML cheaper than global fixed RK4 on 89.2% and than global fixed leapfrog on 98.1% of orbits, at 96.1% in-tolerance for ML (global RK4: 96.1%; global leapfrog: 96.8%). |
| H2 | Certified scales give ≤5% violation rate on the locked audit rows | Point estimates meet 5%; 95% intervals reach above 5% | RK4: 17/500 = 3.40% (Clopper-Pearson 95% CI 1.99% to 5.39%). Leapfrog: 19/498 = 3.82% (CI 2.31% to 5.89%). Without the scale: RK4 11.2%, leapfrog 14.5%, Euler 27.1%. (CIs computed by this report's script, not stored in the result files.) |
| H3 | Is FTLE needed? (removing it lowers RK4 R² or selection accuracy with the whole paired 95% interval below zero) | Not met under the rule | Pinned HGB-quantile model: RK4 R² change -0.2526 (95% CI -0.543 to 0.03776); selection accuracy change 0.007913 (CI -0.008581 to 0.02441). RF sensitivity run: RK4 R² change -0.07033 (CI -0.1428 to 0.002113); selection accuracy change -7.516e-04 (CI -0.01053 to 0.009027). All intervals include zero. |
| H4 | Labels: fraction of orbits with non-monotone pass/fail over a dense step sweep | Reported (no threshold) | 1.5% of 200 orbits (95% CI 0.3% to 4.3%). Median relative disagreement of the halving search vs dense sweep: 0.82%; monotone label vs dense sweep: 0.80%. |
| H5 | Conformal error-model recommender: violation rate ≤10% among covered test orbits | NOT met | Violation rate 17.4% (15 of 86 covered orbits; 95% CI 10.1% to 27.1%); coverage 95.6%; 90 test orbits only. Cheaper than RK45/DOP853 on 0.0% / 0.0% of orbits. |

### 1.2 What this means in plain terms


**The headline.** The ML model does **not** save computation compared with standard adaptive solvers (RK45, DOP853). The preregistered rule for that outcome is: *"ML does not beat adaptive solvers on cost."* The final run's own label is `ML_DOES_NOT_BEAT_ADAPTIVE_ON_COST: do not claim a speed advantage`.

**Why it loses.**
- The ML recommendation is a *fixed* step size, shrunk by a safety factor so that it stays under 100 km error. It averages 15,468.4 force evaluations per orbit; the adaptive solvers need about 1,077.2 (RK45) and 898.1 (DOP853) at the per-orbit oracle tolerance.
- The FTLE feature costs more than a whole adaptive solve (variational FTLE steps cost 7.3× an RK4 step). Dropping it (H1′) removes that cost but model inference still costs about 590.9 force-evaluation equivalents per orbit; the median adaptive solve on the same orbits needs 146 (RK45, oracle rtol) or 122 (DOP853, oracle rtol) evaluations.

**What does work.**
- The calibrated safety layer cuts the violation rate from 11.2% / 14.5% (RK4 / leapfrog, raw) to 3.4% / 3.8% (scaled).
- Against the best *single* fixed step, ML is cheaper on 89% (RK4) and 98% (leapfrog) of orbits. Mean evaluations: ML 15,786.6 vs global RK4 41,874.1.
- Integrator selection beats "always RK4" by a small margin: 89.4% vs 86.8% on the locked set.
- Crash/escape detection with FTLE is strong (AUC 0.9929 vs 0.7801 without). FTLE is integrated over the same horizon as the crash it is asked to predict (sections 9 and 15).
- Within the Sun-Earth system (5,000 orbits), integrator selection reaches 91.8% vs 61.1% for always-RK4 (95% CIs 89.2%-94.4% vs 52.1%-70.0%). This is a within-system result and does not carry over to the other system.
- The numerical methods behave exactly as theory says (slopes 1, 2, 4).

**What does not work.**
- Euler is essentially unpredictable (R² ≈ 0.01754) and is excluded as a candidate (used as a negative control).
- Transfer between systems does not beat the trivial always-RK4 baseline in either direction (section 8): Earth-Moon → Sun-Earth selection accuracy 61.8% vs 61.1%; Sun-Earth → Earth-Moon 81.9% vs 86.1%.
- The conformal error-model recommender violates tolerance more often than its target (section 11).
- The CR3BP model itself differs from a real ephemeris by thousands of km, so a 100 km tolerance only describes integrator error *inside the model* (section 13).


### 1.3 Wall-clock note (read before quoting any speed number)


The ML integration step on its own ran in a mean of 0.001496 s per orbit versus 0.004375 s (oracle rtol) / 0.007062 s (calibrated rtol) for RK45 and 0.003448 s / 0.004654 s for DOP853 (H1 run). That is **not** a like-for-like comparison: the fixed-step code is compiled (Numba) while the adaptive solvers are SciPy, and the project's own code (`fair_baseline_3d.py`) notes that wall-clock comparisons are biased against the adaptive solvers. Once feature extraction and prediction are included, the mean total ML wall time is 0.08888 s (H1 run, FTLE model) and 0.1203 s (H1′ run), i.e. slower than the adaptive solvers. The preregistered cost metric is right-hand-side evaluations, not wall time.


## 2. Glossary and protocol

### 2.1 Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CR3BP | Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem: a tiny body moving under two massive bodies (here Earth and Moon, mass ratio μ = 0.01215058535) that orbit each other in circles. |
| DU / TU | Distance unit (Earth-Moon distance, 384,400 km) and time unit of the normalized system. 1 TU ≈ 4.348 days. |
| dt | Integrator step size in TU. |
| Tolerance (100 km) | 2.6015e-4 DU. An integration "passes" if its position error against a high-accuracy reference stays under 100 km. Illustrative, not a mission requirement. |
| Violation | Error above the tolerance, a collision, an escape, a non-finite result, or a run stopped by the 4,000,000-step cap. |
| Scale (safety factor) | Multiplier applied to the model-predicted step (≤1) so the step is smaller than the predicted largest passing step. Chosen by the certification rule below. |
| Certification (LTT) | For every candidate scale, a one-sided binomial test of "violation rate > α" (α = 0.05) at level δ/m (δ = 0.1, Bonferroni over the m grid values). The largest certified scale is used. Same rule for the ML scales, the global fixed step and the adaptive rtol. |
| Hurdle model | Two models per integrator: a classifier (can any step pass?) and a regressor (largest passing step if so). Regressor here: HistGradientBoosting quantile (q = 0.1) on log10(dt), deliberately aiming low. |
| R² / MAE | R² of the predicted step vs the oracle step; MAE is mean absolute error. I did not verify from the code whether MAE is on dt or log10(dt). |
| Censored | The step-size label is a bound (the search reached its limit) rather than a measured value. This is my reading; check `data_3d.py` for the exact rule. "uncens" metrics use only uncensored rows. |
| FTLE | Finite-time Lyapunov exponent: how fast nearby trajectories separate. Variational version integrates the state-transition matrix along the trajectory. |
| Jacobi drift | Change in the conserved Jacobi constant during a run; a cheap proxy for integration error. |
| Evals / RHS-equivalents | Number of force (right-hand-side) evaluations, the preregistered cost metric. FTLE and model-prediction costs are converted into the same unit. |
| spec / cal | "_spec": adaptive solver at its per-orbit oracle rtol, tuned for each orbit using the known truth (an oracle no real user has, so a lower bound on adaptive cost). "_cal": adaptive solver at one rtol per method (1e-7) chosen on calibration rows with the same certification rule. Unsuffixed (matched-accuracy) columns: adaptive solver tuned per orbit to reach the same final position error as the ML run; not part of the verdict. |
| RK45 / DOP853 | SciPy adaptive Runge-Kutta solvers (orders 5(4) and 8(5,3)). |
| H1 / H1′ / H1′a / H1′b | Cost hypotheses. H1 charges the FTLE feature cost. H1′ uses a model without FTLE and charges prediction cost; H1′a compares against adaptive solvers, H1′b against the best single fixed step. H1′ was added on 2026-10-23 after development data had been seen (documented as a deviation). |
| Locked set | 5,000 of the 20,000 seed-12 orbits, drawn once (seed 2024, 25%) and untouched until the single `final` call; about 4,065 remain usable after reference-divergent rows are dropped. |

### 2.3 Preregistration (verbatim from `PREREGISTRATION.md`)

<details>
<summary>Data and protocol (fixed in advance)</summary>

##### Data and protocol (fixed in advance)
- Systems: Earth-Moon (mu = 0.01215058535). Optional second system for the cross-mu question: Sun-Earth, generated
  with the SAME normalized tolerance (`--tol_du`).
- Tolerance: 100 km Earth-Moon = 100/384400 DU = 2.6015e-4 DU, the same normalized tolerance for Sun-Earth (38,917 km).
  Confirmed: 100 km. It is illustrative, not a mission requirement. The earlier `fidelity` run (CR3BP vs a real ephemeris) gave
  errors of 2,000-50,000 km, so every result here is about integrator error against the CR3BP, not about real trajectories.
  Changing the tolerance means regenerating the datasets.
- Labels: `--label_mode accuracy_monotone` (the only dataset label). The halving ("accuracy") label is computed alongside it
  inside `audit --dense` for H4; no separate accuracy-mode dataset is generated.
- Model (pinned, same in every command: gate, final, audit, ablate, replicate, mu): hurdle models with random-forest classifiers
  (`--n_estimators 150`) and a HistGradientBoosting QUANTILE regressor on log10(dt), quantile 0.1, `--seed 42`.
  `--regressor rf` is allowed only as a labelled sensitivity run (the CLI prints a warning). Quantile 0.1 confirmed; it was chosen
  before any tuning and has not been tuned. Because the regressor aims low on purpose, R^2 against the oracle step and selection accuracy
  are lower than for RF and are not comparable to earlier RF results.
- Certification (ML step scale, global fixed step, adaptive rtol; alpha = 0.05, delta = 0.1): for every value g on a pre-specified grid,
  one-sided binomial test of "violation rate > alpha" with p = P(Binomial(n, alpha) <= observed violations); g is certified if
  p <= delta / m (Bonferroni over the m grid values, no monotonicity assumption); the LARGEST certified g is used. A violation is an error
  above the tolerance, a collision, an escape, a non-finite result, or a run stopped by the 4,000,000-step cap. Grids: scales
  `LTT_SCALE_GRID` (18 values, 0.02-1.0), global steps `GLOBAL_DT_GRID` (50 values, 1e-4-0.49), adaptive rtol 1e-12-1e-2 in half decades.
  An adaptive (RK45/DOP853) solve that needs more than 2,000,000 right-hand-side evaluations is abandoned: it counts as a violation while
  calibrating the rtol, and in the cost comparison the orbit is skipped (counted in `n_skipped`; `adaptive_cap_hits_total` is reported).
  Without this cap a single orbit with a very close approach stalled a test comparison for over an hour.
- Splits: `gate` and `final` train on a random 70% of the development rows (`--split random`, pinned) and calibrate on rows from the
  held-out 30%, so calibration rows are drawn like the locked rows and never used for training. `--split grouped` is a stress test only.
  Other commands keep the grouped (region-shift) split, which answers a different question.
- Datasets (label pipeline version 3, SeedSequence seeding; SHA-256 recorded in each run's manifest and in `FREEZE.json`):
  - Earth-Moon, 20,000 orbits each, base seeds 12 (primary: development plus the locked set), 13 and 15 (replication):
    `data/cr3bp_3d_training_data_accuracy_monotone_seed{12,13,15}.csv`
    (sha256 15bc463aa6dd2caf8b325ff13120e94a4f52635a35228327c50b547256e0532e, 38fb401b9f3807979869a82ac97ecbea553d9e9ba79fd936fadbf1c8240660d6,
    7de9acef8b5872086fc3d3c3a2da1f5bf38751ff7e394e7b8e82d167c1899a61).
  - Sun-Earth (mu = 3.00348e-6), 5,000 orbits, base seed 14, for the cross-mu question:
    `data/cr3bp_3d_training_mu_0.000003_accuracy_monotone_seed14.csv`
    (sha256 1a39b6e40b66d5a3ca414ac300f292ddaf8ad5bcf2003d808efe1ae4fbd295fb).
- Locked test set: drawn once with `lock` (seed 2024, fraction 0.25, random) from the seed-12 CSV into `data/locked_test_set.json`
  (5,000 of 20,000 rows; about 4,060 are usable after reference-divergent rows are dropped, leaving about 12,180 usable development rows);
  evaluated by `final` only after every development decision is made. Every `final` call is logged; report the number of calls.
  A `final` that has to be repeated (for example after a bug) needs a dated reason under "Deviations".



</details>

<details>
<summary>Hypotheses and decision rules H1-H7</summary>

##### Hypotheses and decision rules
H1 (cost). On the locked set, the ML recommendation (candidate integrators RK4 and leapfrog, certified safety scale,
FTLE feature cost INCLUDED; model prediction cost is charged only in H1', in H1 it is reported as wall time) meets the tolerance in >= 90% of orbits AND needs fewer
right-hand-side-equivalent evaluations than each of RK45 and DOP853 in >= 50% of orbits, against BOTH the per-orbit
oracle rtol ("_spec") and the calibrated rtol ("_cal"). H1 is supported only if all evaluated comparisons pass.
Otherwise report: "ML does not beat adaptive solvers on cost."

H1' (cost, no-FTLE variant; added 2026-10-23, see Deviations). Same orbits, tolerance, calibration rows, alpha/delta and
thresholds as H1 (meets the tolerance in >= 90% of orbits AND needs fewer right-hand-side-equivalent evaluations in >= 50%),
but with (i) a model trained WITHOUT the FTLE feature (same regressor and quantile as H1), (ii) feature cost charged at
1 RHS-equivalent for the remaining state-derived features, and (iii) the model's batched inference cost charged
(`ml_total_evals_equiv_pred`, measured wall-time ratio to one compiled RHS evaluation). Judged in two parts, each on its own:
- H1'a (vs adaptive): against RK45 and DOP853, both the per-orbit oracle rtol ("_spec") and the calibrated rtol ("_cal").
  Supported only if all four comparisons pass.
- H1'b (vs global fixed step): against the best SINGLE fixed step per integrator (RK4, leapfrog), certified on the same
  calibration rows with the same alpha/delta and the same certification rule as the ML scales (see "Certification"; a collision,
  escape or step-cap run counts as a violation). Supported only if both comparisons pass.
A part (and H1 itself) is supported only if EVERY comparison in it was evaluated and passed. If any evaluated comparison fails it is
reported as not supported (with the number of comparisons that could not be evaluated, e.g. because an rtol or step could not be
certified). If none fails but at least one could not be evaluated it is reported NOT_FULLY_EVALUATED, never as supported on a subset.
The original H1 is still run and reported with its original comparisons. H1 and H1' are reported together.

H2 (safety). The certified scales (alpha = 0.05, delta = 0.1, rule under "Certification", calibrated on rows exchangeable with the
locked rows) give a violation rate <= 5% on the locked audit rows;
report the Clopper-Pearson interval, and the spread of the chosen scale over calibration repeats (`audit --ltt_repeats`).

H3 (is FTLE needed). In `ablate`, FTLE is "needed" if the paired 95% interval of the change in `rk4_r2_uncens`
or `selection_acc_no_euler` when it is removed lies entirely below zero. If it is needed, its cost is charged to the ML
side (already done in `gate`). H3 is evaluated with the pinned regressor; an RF run of `ablate` is also reported as a sensitivity check.

H4 (labels). Report the fraction of orbits with non-monotone pass/fail over the dense sweep (n >= 200) with its
interval, and the relative disagreement between the halving label and the monotone label.

H5 (error model). The conformal error-model recommender has violation rate <= 10% among covered test orbits; report
coverage and cost versus adaptive solvers as in H1.

H6 (crash/escape). Report accuracy, balanced accuracy, recall and AUC with and without the FTLE feature, and recall by
outcome type. No pass/fail threshold.

H7 (convergence). Report median fitted slopes per integrator and region against the textbook orders (Euler 1,
leapfrog 2, RK4 4). No pass/fail threshold; deviations are findings.



</details>

<details>
<summary>Which data evaluates what; run plan; reported regardless of outcome</summary>

##### Which data evaluates what
- Lock guard: a CSV that has a `locked_test_set*.json` next to it (matched by the CSV's SHA-256) is refused by every command unless
  `--locked` points at that file. `--ignore_lock` overrides this, prints a warning and is recorded in the run's `manifest.json`;
  nothing computed with it may be used for a claim about the locked set.
- Locked set (via `final`, once): H1, H1' and the locked audit for H2.
- Development rows only (every command run with `--locked data/locked_test_set.json` so locked rows are excluded): H3 (`ablate`),
  H4 and the calibration-stability part of H2 (`audit`), H5 (`errmodel`), H6 (`crash`), H7 (`convergence`), `proxy`, and `gate`.
- Replication and cross-mu: `replicate` (seeds 12, 13, 15) and `mu` (seed 12 vs the Sun-Earth seed 14); `--locked` removes the locked rows of the
  seed-12 dataset from these. `replicate` trains on a random 70% of dataset A and reports "within" (the other 30% of A) next to "replicate"
  (the same model on every row of independent dataset B); `replicate_minus_within` is the dataset-to-dataset effect. The grouped
  (region-shift) score is reported separately as `within_grouped` and is not comparable with the other two.

##### Run plan (all from this folder with the base conda python; pinned arguments, defaults otherwise)
```
D12=data/cr3bp_3d_training_data_accuracy_monotone_seed12.csv   # likewise D13, D15; S14=data/cr3bp_3d_training_mu_0.000003_accuracy_monotone_seed14.csv
L=data/locked_test_set.json
python3 freeze_snapshot.py snapshot ; <fill placeholders> ; python3 freeze_snapshot.py seal
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py lock      --data $D12 --locked_out $L --lock_seed 2024 --lock_frac 0.25 --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py audit     --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --seeds 10 --audit_rows 100 --ltt_rows 600 --ltt_repeats 10 --tol_sens 50 --dense 200 --halo --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py ablate    --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --seeds 5 --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py ablate    --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --seeds 5 --regressor rf --out_dir out   # sensitivity
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py crash     --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --seeds 5 --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py proxy     --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py errmodel  --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --n_orbits 300 --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py convergence --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --n_orbits 300 --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py replicate --dataset s12=$D12 --dataset s13=$D13 --dataset s15=$D15 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --seeds 5 --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py mu        --dataset EarthMoon=$D12 --dataset SunEarth=$S14 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --seeds 5 --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py fidelity  --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --out_dir out        # needs network + astroquery
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py gate      --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --out_dir out
python3 run_rigor_suite_3d.py final     --data $D12 --locked $L --prereg PREREGISTRATION.md --out_dir out    # once
```

## Deviations", SHA-256 of the data CSVs). After the seal,

Frozen on: `2026-10-23`. Student: `Arnav Deopura`. Code snapshot SHA-256: `79a6455ddef80ac312af267d14d952d3facb3e9c6b6f0c7dd752b794c61968e1`.

##### Data and protocol (fixed in advance)
- Systems: Earth-Moon (mu = 0.01215058535). Optional second system for the cross-mu question: Sun-Earth, generated
  with the SAME normalized tolerance (`--tol_du`).
- Tolerance: 100 km Earth-Moon = 100/384400 DU = 2.6015e-4 DU, the same normalized tolerance for Sun-Earth (38,917 km).
  Confirmed: 100 km. It is illustrative, not a mission requirement. The earlier `fidelity` run (CR3BP vs a real ephemeris) gave
  errors of 2,000-50,000 km, so every result here is about integrator error against the CR3BP, not about real trajectories.
  Changing the tolerance means regenerating the datasets.
- Labels: `--label_mode accuracy_monotone` (the only dataset label). The halving ("accuracy") label is computed alongside it
  inside `audit --dense` for H4; no separate accuracy-mode dataset is generated.
- Model (pinned, same in every command: gate, final, audit, ablate, replicate, mu): hurdle models with random-forest classifiers
  (`--n_estimators 150`) and a HistGradientBoosting QUANTILE regressor on log10(dt), quantile 0.1, `--seed 42`.
  `--regressor rf` is allowed only as a labelled sensitivity run (the CLI prints a warning). Quantile 0.1 confirmed; it was chosen
  before any tuning and has not been tuned. Because the regressor aims low on purpose, R^2 against the oracle step and selection accuracy
  are lower than for RF and are not comparable to earlier RF results.
- Certification (ML step scale, global fixed step, adaptive rtol; alpha = 0.05, delta = 0.1): for every value g on a pre-specified grid,
  one-sided binomial test of "violation rate > alpha" with p = P(Binomial(n, alpha) <= observed violations); g is certified if
  p <= delta / m (Bonferroni over the m grid values, no monotonicity assumption); the LARGEST certified g is used. A violation is an error
  above the tolerance, a collision, an escape, a non-finite result, or a run stopped by the 4,000,000-step cap. Grids: scales
  `LTT_SCALE_GRID` (18 values, 0.02-1.0), global steps `GLOBAL_DT_GRID` (50 values, 1e-4-0.49), adaptive rtol 1e-12-1e-2 in half decades.
  An adaptive (RK45/DOP853) solve that needs more than 2,000,000 right-hand-side evaluations is abandoned: it counts as a violation while
  calibrating the rtol, and in the cost comparison the orbit is skipped (counted in `n_skipped`; `adaptive_cap_hits_total` is reported).
  Without this cap a single orbit with a very close approach stalled a test comparison for over an hour.
- Splits: `gate` and `final` train on a random 70% of the development rows (`--split random`, pinned) and calibrate on rows from the
  held-out 30%, so calibration rows are drawn like the locked rows and never used for training. `--split grouped` is a stress test only.
  Other commands keep the grouped (region-shift) split, which answers a different question.
- Datasets (label pipeline version 3, SeedSequence seeding; SHA-256 recorded in each run's manifest and in `FREEZE.json`):
  - Earth-Moon, 20,000 orbits each, base seeds 12 (primary: development plus the locked set), 13 and 15 (replication):
    `data/cr3bp_3d_training_data_accuracy_monotone_seed{12,13,15}.csv`
    (sha256 15bc463aa6dd2caf8b325ff13120e94a4f52635a35228327c50b547256e0532e, 38fb401b9f3807979869a82ac97ecbea553d9e9ba79fd936fadbf1c8240660d6,
    7de9acef8b5872086fc3d3c3a2da1f5bf38751ff7e394e7b8e82d167c1899a61).
  - Sun-Earth (mu = 3.00348e-6), 5,000 orbits, base seed 14, for the cross-mu question:
    `data/cr3bp_3d_training_mu_0.000003_accuracy_monotone_seed14.csv`
    (sha256 1a39b6e40b66d5a3ca414ac300f292ddaf8ad5bcf2003d808efe1ae4fbd295fb).
- Locked test set: drawn once with `lock` (seed 2024, fraction 0.25, random) from the seed-12 CSV into `data/locked_test_set.json`
  (5,000 of 20,000 rows; about 4,060 are usable after reference-divergent rows are dropped, leaving about 12,180 usable development rows);
  evaluated by `final` only after every development decision is made. Every `final` call is logged; report the number of calls.
  A `final` that has to be repeated (for example after a bug) needs a dated reason under "Deviations".

##### Hypotheses and decision rules
H1 (cost). On the locked set, the ML recommendation (candidate integrators RK4 and leapfrog, certified safety scale,
FTLE feature cost INCLUDED; model prediction cost is charged only in H1', in H1 it is reported as wall time) meets the tolerance in >= 90% of orbits AND needs fewer
right-hand-side-equivalent evaluations than each of RK45 and DOP853 in >= 50% of orbits, against BOTH the per-orbit
oracle rtol ("_spec") and the calibrated rtol ("_cal"). H1 is supported only if all evaluated comparisons pass.
Otherwise report: "ML does not beat adaptive solvers on cost."

H1' (cost, no-FTLE variant; added 2026-10-23, see Deviations). Same orbits, tolerance, calibration rows, alpha/delta and
thresholds as H1 (meets the tolerance in >= 90% of orbits AND needs fewer right-hand-side-equivalent evaluations in >= 50%),
but with (i) a model trained WITHOUT the FTLE feature (same regressor and quantile as H1), (ii) feature cost charged at
1 RHS-equivalent for the remaining state-derived features, and (iii) the model's batched inference cost charged
(`ml_total_evals_equiv_pred`, measured wall-time ratio to one compiled RHS evaluation). Judged in two parts, each on its own:
- H1'a (vs adaptive): against RK45 and DOP853, both the per-orbit oracle rtol ("_spec") and the calibrated rtol ("_cal").
  Supported only if all four comparisons pass.
- H1'b (vs global fixed step): against the best SINGLE fixed step per integrator (RK4, leapfrog), certified on the same
  calibration rows with the same alpha/delta and the same certification rule as the ML scales (see "Certification"; a collision,
  escape or step-cap run counts as a violation). Supported only if both comparisons pass.
A part (and H1 itself) is supported only if EVERY comparison in it was evaluated and passed. If any evaluated comparison fails it is
reported as not supported (with the number of comparisons that could not be evaluated, e.g. because an rtol or step could not be
certified). If none fails but at least one could not be evaluated it is reported NOT_FULLY_EVALUATED, never as supported on a subset.
The original H1 is still run and reported with its original comparisons. H1 and H1' are reported together.

H2 (safety). The certified scales (alpha = 0.05, delta = 0.1, rule under "Certification", calibrated on rows exchangeable with the
locked rows) give a violation rate <= 5% on the locked audit rows;
report the Clopper-Pearson interval, and the spread of the chosen scale over calibration repeats (`audit --ltt_repeats`).

H3 (is FTLE needed). In `ablate`, FTLE is "needed" if the paired 95% interval of the change in `rk4_r2_uncens`
or `selection_acc_no_euler` when it is removed lies entirely below zero. If it is needed, its cost is charged to the ML
side (already done in `gate`). H3 is evaluated with the pinned regressor; an RF run of `ablate` is also reported as a sensitivity check.

H4 (labels). Report the fraction of orbits with non-monotone pass/fail over the dense sweep (n >= 200) with its
interval, and the relative disagreement between the halving label and the monotone label.

H5 (error model). The conformal error-model recommender has violation rate <= 10% among covered test orbits; report
coverage and cost versus adaptive solvers as in H1.

H6 (crash/escape). Report accuracy, balanced accuracy, recall and AUC with and without the FTLE feature, and recall by
outcome type. No pass/fail threshold.

H7 (convergence). Report median fitted slopes per integrator and region against the textbook orders (Euler 1,
leapfrog 2, RK4 4). No pass/fail threshold; deviations are findings.

##### Which data evaluates what
- Lock guard: a CSV that has a `locked_test_set*.json` next to it (matched by the CSV's SHA-256) is refused by every command unless
  `--locked` points at that file. `--ignore_lock` overrides this, prints a warning and is recorded in the run's `manifest.json`;
  nothing computed with it may be used for a claim about the locked set.
- Locked set (via `final`, once): H1, H1' and the locked audit for H2.
- Development rows only (every command run with `--locked data/locked_test_set.json` so locked rows are excluded): H3 (`ablate`),
  H4 and the calibration-stability part of H2 (`audit`), H5 (`errmodel`), H6 (`crash`), H7 (`convergence`), `proxy`, and `gate`.
- Replication and cross-mu: `replicate` (seeds 12, 13, 15) and `mu` (seed 12 vs the Sun-Earth seed 14); `--locked` removes the locked rows of the
  seed-12 dataset from these. `replicate` trains on a random 70% of dataset A and reports "within" (the other 30% of A) next to "replicate"
  (the same model on every row of independent dataset B); `replicate_minus_within` is the dataset-to-dataset effect. The grouped
  (region-shift) score is reported separately as `within_grouped` and is not comparable with the other two.

##### Reported regardless of outcome
All of H1-H7, including negative results; the number of orbits skipped in each comparison; Euler as a negative control.

##### Deviations (date, what, why)
- 2026-10-23 (before the freeze): replaced the fixed-sequence-from-the-smallest-value certification with Bonferroni over the grid (largest
  certified value), for the ML scales, the global fixed step and the adaptive rtol alike. Why: the earlier rule stopped at the first
  non-rejection, and step-cap runs counted as violations make the smallest scale the worst one (leapfrog 2.7% step-cap failures at scale
  0.02 in a 300-row test; 5-13% in the previous run), so nothing could be certified. Cost: each value needs p <= 0.1/m, a small loss of power.
  Also before the freeze: `gate`/`final` now use a random train/held-out split (the grouped split put the calibration rows in different
  regions than the random locked rows); `replicate` compares like with like; the original H1 verdict can no longer be "competitive" on a subset
  of its comparisons. A failed comparison now outranks missing ones in both H1 and H1'.
  Also before the freeze: adaptive solves are capped at 2,000,000 RHS evaluations (see Certification).
- 2026-10-23 (before the freeze): corrected the wording of H1 and the Data section to match the implemented cost basis. The earlier draft said
  H1 includes "prediction cost", but the code (`ml_total_evals_equiv`) only ever charged the FTLE feature; prediction cost is charged only in
  H1' (`ml_total_evals_equiv_pred`). Also removed the "accuracy (secondary)" dataset (never generated; H4 uses `audit --dense`), and filled in
  seeds, locked-set parameters, tolerance and quantile (accepted as proposed).
- 2026-10-23: added H1'a and H1'b (and the code behind them: `--no_h1_prime` off by default in `gate`/`final`,
  `calibrate_global_dt_ltt`, `measure_prediction_cost`). Why: on development data (Earth-Moon seed 12, 80 sampled orbits) the FTLE feature
  alone cost more than a whole DOP853 solve in 80/80 orbits (median ~70x), and `gate`/`final` always charge it, so H1 as written
  cannot be supported regardless of safety quality. Also seen before writing this (post hoc, development data only; the locked set
  did not exist): with an oracle step size, free features and free prediction, ML was cheaper than DOP853 at rtol 3.2e-7 in 37% / 24% / 8%
  of orbits at safety scales 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.4, and batched model inference was measured at ~730 RHS-equivalents per orbit (RK4 + leapfrog,
  hgb_quantile regressors + RF classifiers) against a median DOP853 solve of ~254 evaluations, so H1'a is expected to fail; H1'b was
  added because the adaptive solvers are not the only comparator a user of fixed-step integrators has. H1 itself is unchanged.
- 2026-10-23: pinned the regressor (hgb_quantile, quantile 0.1) as the default for gate, final, audit, ablate, replicate and mu, and added
  `--regressor/--quantile` to ablate, replicate and mu (+ `model_kw` in `rigor_3d.py`). Why: in the previous run `gate` used hgb_quantile but
  `final` used rf, so the locked evaluation did not test the model that was developed. Measured on development data (Earth-Moon seed 12, 2 seeds):
  rk4_r2_uncens 0.65-0.83 (rf) vs 0.19-0.60 (hgb_quantile); selection_acc_no_euler 0.92-0.97 vs 0.89-0.94 (majority baseline ~0.90); removing FTLE
  changed rk4_r2_uncens by -0.10 (rf) and -0.28 (hgb_quantile), same sign. `crash` is unaffected (it fits no hurdle regressor).

### 3.8 Locked-set safety audit (H2)

Each audited orbit is re-integrated with the recommended step. "Unscaled" uses the raw model prediction; "scaled" applies the certified safety scale. Violation counts are back-calculated from the stored rate × n; Clopper-Pearson intervals are computed by this report's script (they are not in the result file).

## 4. Gate run (development rehearsal of the final test)

Run `gate_20261024T001012Z`. Same protocol as the final run but on development rows only (calibration and test rows come from the development pool, the locked set excluded). The run plan places it immediately before `final`. Its results agree with the final run (compare the two overall labels: gate `ML_DOES_NOT_BEAT_ADAPTIVE_ON_COST: do not claim a speed advantage`, final `ML_DOES_NOT_BEAT_ADAPTIVE_ON_COST: do not claim a speed advantage`).

## 5. Audit

Run `audit_20261023T232014Z` (development rows only; locked rows excluded). It checks how stable the certified scale is when the calibration sample changes, whether the step-size labels are monotone, how the model does across 10 seeds, how it behaves on analytic halo orbits, and how step sizes change with tolerance.

## 6. Feature ablation (H3)

Question: which input features matter? "full" uses all features; "no_ftle" removes FTLE; "state_only" keeps only raw position/velocity/time; each "drop_*" removes one feature. Five seeds, grouped split on development rows. **Primary run = the pinned regressor (HistGradientBoosting quantile 0.1).** The RF run is the preregistered sensitivity check. `drop_ftle_3d` and `no_ftle` give identical numbers because they are the same feature set.

H3 rule: FTLE is "needed" if the paired 95% interval of the change in `rk4_r2_uncens` or `selection_acc_no_euler` lies entirely below zero. Result: pinned run **not met**, RF run **not met**.

## 7. Replication across independent datasets

Three Earth-Moon datasets of 20,000 orbits generated with different seeds (12, 13, 15; locked rows removed from seed 12). "within": train on 70% of dataset A, test on the other 30% of A. "replicate": same model tested on all rows of independent dataset B. "within_grouped": region-shift split (not comparable with the others). "replicate minus within" isolates the dataset-to-dataset effect.

## 9. Crash / escape prediction (H6)

Binary question: will the orbit end in a collision or escape (a failure no step size can fix)? Classifier with and without the FTLE feature; five seeds, grouped split on development rows. No pass/fail threshold was preregistered. **Caveat (from the project's own code, `outcome_3d.py`):** the FTLE feature comes from integrating the variational equations over the same horizon, so for a crashing trajectory the FTLE input has already "seen" the crash; the with-FTLE result is therefore not a prediction from the initial state alone.

## 10. Error proxy (Jacobi drift) and error predictor

Question: can a cheap by-product of a run (drift of the conserved Jacobi constant) tell us whether the position error exceeded the tolerance? "False assurance" = drift looks fine but the error is over tolerance. "False alarm" = drift looks bad but the error is fine.

## 11. Conformal error-model recommender (H5)

Alternative recommender: predict the position error of each integrator/step and add a conformal margin (miscoverage α = 0.1). ## 12. Convergence orders (H7)

For each orbit the step is halved repeatedly and the slope of log(error) vs log(step) is fitted. A method of order p should give slope p. "frac_within_half_order" is the share of fits within ±0.5 of the theoretical order.

Overall by integrator (the three rows with `grouping = integrator`) are the headline: Euler 1.0003, leapfrog 2.0000, RK4 4.0170.

## 13. Fidelity: CR3BP vs real ephemeris

How far does the CR3BP drift from a real trajectory? Data: JPL Horizons states for the CAPSTONE spacecraft (Horizons ID -1176) and the Moon, 2023-01-01 to 2023-01-15 at 6-hour steps. Each state is converted to the CR3BP synodic frame; the CR3BP is propagated from epoch i with DOP853 and the position difference to the observed state at later epochs is reported by lag. This is the size of the *model* error that exists regardless of integrator. Three scenarios vary the CR3BP time unit by ±1% (nominal 4.3484 days = sidereal month / 2π).

Caveats stated in the code (`fidelity_3d.py`): the synodic frame is rebuilt at every epoch from the Moon's instantaneous state, so part of the lunar eccentricity is absorbed; a 1% change in the time unit alone moves the apparent model error by thousands of km at 1-2 TU lag; only Earth+Moon gravity is modelled (no Sun, solar-radiation pressure or non-spherical gravity); and the real spacecraft may have performed maneuvers inside the window. One spacecraft over 14 days is a single case study.

## 15. Limitations and things to check

| Issue | Detail |
|---|---|
| Model error dwarfs the tolerance | CR3BP vs the CAPSTONE ephemeris differs by a median of 2,065.7 km at lags up to 0.25 TU, rising to 50,046.2 km at 3-5 TU, against a 100 km integration tolerance. Results describe integrator error inside the CR3BP, not accuracy for real trajectories. Single spacecraft, 14-day window, stated caveats in section 13. |
| Adaptive solvers are the right comparator and they win | The ML output is a fixed step with a worst-case safety factor, so it cannot match a solver that adapts its step along the orbit. No post-hoc subgroup (section 3.6) was a regime where ML wins. |
| FTLE has two problems | (a) It costs more than a whole adaptive solve on the development sample (preregistration deviation note: median ≈70×). (b) The code itself flags that FTLE is integrated over the same horizon as the trajectory it is used to predict, so it is not a pre-simulation feature for crash/escape prediction. For the step-size task, removing FTLE changed RK4 R² by -0.2526 (CI -0.543 to 0.03776) and selection accuracy by 0.007913 (CI -0.008581 to 0.02441). |
| Safety intervals reach above 5% | Scaled violation rates are 3.40% (RK4) and 3.82% (leapfrog) with 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bounds of 5.39% and 5.89%. The point estimates meet 5%; the intervals do not rule out more. |
| Failures can be large | Worst-case errors in the scaled locked audit reach 848,681.5 km (RK4) and 51,803.0 km (leapfrog), so the safety layer limits how often errors exceed tolerance, not how large the worst error can be. |
| Cost test uses a subsample | The H1 cost comparison covers 996 orbits (4 skipped because an adaptive solve exceeded the 2,000,000-evaluation cap; 17 cap hits in total) out of 4065 usable locked orbits. |
| Post-hoc additions | H1′, H1′a, H1′b and the regime breakdown were added after development data had been seen (dated deviations in the preregistration). H1′b in particular is a favourable comparator for ML. |
| Small samples in some analyses | Error-model recommender: 90 test orbits. Crash classifier and ablations: 5 seeds with wide intervals. Proxy analysis: 40/29/29 train/cal/test orbits. Sun-Earth set: 5,000 orbits. |
| Selection gain is small on Earth-Moon and does not transfer | Locked-set selection accuracy 89.4% vs 86.8% for always-RK4. Cross-system transfer does not beat always-RK4 in either direction (Earth-Moon to Sun-Earth 61.8% vs 61.1%; Sun-Earth to Earth-Moon 81.9% vs 86.1%). The large within-system gain on Sun-Earth (91.8% vs 61.1%) is at least partly because always-RK4 is a weak baseline there (RK4 is the best choice for only about 61% of Sun-Earth orbits; my reading). |
| Many RK4 labels hit the search ceiling | In the 50-orbit tolerance-sensitivity sample (section 5.4), the RK4 step-size label is censored (at the maximum step 0.5) for 36% of orbits at 100 km (leapfrog: 2%). For those orbits the label is a lower bound, which is why R² is reported both for all rows and for uncensored rows. |
| Euler is excluded | Euler is unpredictable (R² ≈ 0) and fails the tolerance in most orbits; it is kept only as a negative control, so the integrator choice is effectively RK4 vs leapfrog. |
| Two ablation runs differ in magnitude | The pinned HGB-quantile run and the RF sensitivity run agree in sign but not in size (e.g. removing FTLE: RK4 R² change -0.2526 vs -0.07033). Quote the pinned run, mention the other as sensitivity. |
| Wall-time numbers are implementation-dependent | Compiled Numba fixed-step code vs SciPy adaptive solvers is not a fair wall-time comparison; the preregistered metric is force evaluations. |
| Low-quantile regressor | The regressor aims at the 10th percentile on purpose, so R² against the oracle step and selection accuracy are lower than for a mean-seeking model and are not comparable with earlier RF results. |
| Duplicate file | `error_ladder_table.csv` in the convergence and errmodel runs is byte-identical (True). |

Items I could not verify from the result files alone: the exact definition of the MAE columns (dt vs log10 dt), the exact rule for "censored" labels, and what `covered` means in the error-model evaluation. Check `modeling_3d.py`, `data_3d.py` and `error_model_3d.py` before quoting those.
